bugs.actual: The DUT gave result=0x80, Z=0, C=0, V=0, N=1, which is spec-correct. The test expected flag_n=0.
bugs.evidence: Failure message: inputs a=0x80 b=0x00 op=6(SHR); expected result=128 flag_n=0; actual result=0x80 N=1; only flag_n differs. Spec REQ-007: 'flag_n <= bit 7 of the 8-bit operation result, for every op'. 0x80>>0 = 0x80 has bit 7 = 1. tb/ref_model.py sets flag_n=(opres>>7)&1 (gives 1). formal_top.sv sets ref_n=ref_opres[7] (gives 1). The same test's directed corner (0xFF, n=0) expects flag_n=1, which contradicts the sweep's hard-coded 0. The failure is identical across both simulators and all seeds, so it is deterministic and does not depend on the simulator.
bugs.expected: For op=SHR, a=0x80, b=0x00 (n=0): result=0x80, flag_z=0, flag_c=0, flag_v=0, flag_n=1 (bit 7 of result).
failures: verilator seed 1: test_shr_exhaustive cycle 32771 (a=0x80 b=0x00 op=SHR) differing flag_n
verilator seed 2: test_shr_exhaustive cycle 32771 (a=0x80 b=0x00 op=SHR) differing flag_n
verilator seed 3: test_shr_exhaustive cycle 32771 (a=0x80 b=0x00 op=SHR) differing flag_n
icarus seed 1: test_shr_exhaustive cycle 32771 (a=0x80 b=0x00 op=SHR) differing flag_n
bugs.root_cause: test_shr_exhaustive's sweep loop hard-codes the expected flag_n to 0 for every SHR vector. That holds only for n>=1. For n=0 the result equals a, so flag_n must equal a[7] (REQ-007).
bugs.requirement: REQ-007 (flag_n = bit 7 of the 8-bit operation result for every op), with REQ-005 (SHR by n=b[2:0], n=0 is identity)
bugs.suggested_fix: In the per-vector check of test_shr_exhaustive, set the expected flag_n from the spec instead of the constant 0: flag_n = bit 7 of the expected result ((a >> n) >> 7) & 1. This gives a[7] for n=0 and 0 for n>=1 (REQ-007). Leave every other expected field and the full 65,536-vector sweep unchanged; this makes the check stricter, not weaker. Then re-run test_shr_exhaustive on verilator and icarus to confirm.
